A 77-year-old man presents to the emergency department acutely obtunded.
He has a past medical history of hypothyroidism, depression, and diabetes.
The patient is cold to the touch and moves all extremities to painful stimuli.
His temperature is 88.0°F (31.1°C), blood pressure is 92/62 mmHg, pulse is 35/min, respirations are 9/min, and oxygen saturation is 92% on room air.
His pupils are reactive and sluggish, and he does not follow commands.
He has not been responding to phone calls for the past 3 days.
There are no signs of trauma or skin infections.
The patient is unable to offer a history.
Generally, the patient manages his own finances, medications, and works part-time.
The patient lives alone and was found unresponsive by his son.
